title: Citi Stands Behind 2 Crypto Stocks as Its Top Picks for the Rest of 2026
detail:
Citi Stands Behind 2 Crypto Stocks as Its Top Picks for the Rest of 2026
TipRanks
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:30 AM PDT 8 min read
BTC-USD
C
BLSH
CRCL
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Cryptocurrencies have experienced substantial price swings over the past year, with Bitcoin climbing above $90,000, falling to $60,000, and then recovering to more than $80,000. Despite the volatility, the broader crypto market has regained considerable ground in recent months.

By the end of September, the cryptocurrency market was valued at nearly $3 trillion, while Bitcoin had gained 40% during the third quarter alone. Stronger trading activity and improving capital market conditions have contributed to the recovery, creating a more favorable environment for companies operating in the digital asset industry.

Citi analyst Peter Christiansen believes the improving conditions could benefit companies involved in cryptocurrency infrastructure, particularly those supporting tokenization, stablecoins, and digital financial services.

"Digital assets enter earnings season with a considerably stronger backdrop than just a few months ago. Crypto markets recovered sharply during 3Q26, institutional ETF flows turned positive, and activity across exchanges, stablecoins, and digital asset infrastructure improved. At the same time, regulatory progress continues despite legislative setbacks, with the SEC increasingly advancing digital asset market structure through existing authority. We believe investors are also beginning to look beyond crypto prices and focus more on the infrastructure underpinning tokenization, stablecoins, custody, settlement, and digital capital markets. Against this backdrop, we remain constructive on companies positioned around tokenization and market infrastructure," Christiansen stated.

With that outlook in mind, Christiansen has selected two cryptocurrency stocks as his top picks for the rest of the year. Using data from the TipRanks platform, we'll take a closer look at both companies and examine why the analyst sees further upside ahead.

Circle Internet Group (CRCL)

The first crypto stock we'll look at is Circle Internet Group, an industry leader in the use of digital stablecoins as an internationally acceptable store of value. Like traditional cryptos, stablecoins are based on blockchain technology; unlike traditional cryptos, stablecoins are usually pinned to a known asset – such as US dollars, Euros, or gold – to provide insulation from the sector's volatility. Circle has made use of this to build itself up as a global financial technology provider, offering enterprise clients at all scales access to digital currencies and public blockchains, and advantages in payments, online commerce, and global financial applications.

title: Ranking America's 4 Biggest Banks From Best Buy to Worst
detail:
Ranking America's 4 Biggest Banks From Best Buy to Worst
Bram Berkowitz, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:50 AM PDT 6 min read
NVDA
JPM
BAC
C
WFC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Since the Great Recession in 2008, banking has not exactly been the most attractive sector to invest in.

The blow-up in 2008 caused significant reputational damage, which has taken a long time to recover from. Banks have also faced heightened regulations and the constant need to invest in technology, while also trying to ward off competition from fintech companies.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The four largest banks in the U.S. are JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM), Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), Citigroup (NYSE: C), and Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC). These money-center banks are essentially now too big to fail. They have also developed scale in many core banking businesses that will be difficult to replicate.

Here they are, ranked from best buy to worst.

Image source: Getty Images.
1. JPMorgan Chase

JPMorgan Chase is the largest bank by assets in the U.S., with nearly $5.1 trillion in assets at the end of the third quarter.

JPMorgan Chase is a best-in-breed large-bank stock, run by CEO Jamie Dimon, long regarded as the industry's best CEO. The bank excels in all facets of banking, including credit card lending, investment banking, trading, payments, commercial lending, and asset and wealth management.

The bank also generates returns on tangible common equity (ROTCE) at the top of its peer group. Management has guided for a long-term ROTCE of 17% through a full economic cycle. But the bank typically generates over a 20% ROTCE, and sometimes much higher.

This is no secret, and, as such, the bank has been awarded a premium valuation based on a price-to-tangible book value (TBV) per-share basis, a common way banks are valued.

JPM Price-to-Tangible Book Value data by YCharts.

So, while JPMorgan Chase may have less near-term appreciation, I still like it best in the long term. It's going to consistently put up industry-leading returns and be the most consistent through the cycle.

2. Citigroup

After years of lagging returns, Jane Fraser took the reins at Citigroup in 2021 and implemented a massive turnaround effort that has paid off.

Fraser sold off international consumer banking divisions that lacked the scale to compete and focused on the bank's best-performing businesses, such as investment banking and payments.

In 2027, the bank will complete the lengthy effort to divest the consumer, small-business, and middle-market banking operations of its large division in Mexico, known as Banamex. Citigroup has already sold nearly half of this division, but will conduct an initial public offering for the rest in 2027, still retaining some ownership.

title: Citigroup Posts Solid Q3 as Lower Expenses Drive Earnings Beat, Oppenheimer Says
detail:
PREMIUM
Citigroup Posts Solid Q3 as Lower Expenses Drive Earnings Beat, Oppenheimer Says
MT Newswires
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:12 AM PDT 1 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup's (C) Q3 results were "solid," with better-than-expected earnings driven largely by lower expenses and improving profitability in services and wealth management, Oppenheimer said in a report Thursday.

Citigroup posted earnings per share of $2.85, above its $2.66 estimate and consensus, while revenue of $23.8 billion was broadly in line with expectations. Expenses of $14 billion came in below Oppenheimer's $14.5 billion estimate, helping "pre-provision earnings" rise 17.9% from a year earlier.

The firm said there was "nothing not to like" in the quarter, noting services net income rose 27% year over year and wealth management net income increased 93%. The firm added that results were not "unduly dependent on trading," while credit quality remained stable.

Oppenheimer raised 2027 estimates by 4.6% and said Citi's improving profitability matters more than debate over its target CET1 ratio, according to the report.

Oppenheimer maintained a perform rating on Citigroup, while calling it a "top pick" among universal banks.

title: FMC Stock Crashes 33% On Massive Earnings Downgrade – Citi expects ‘Modest Negative Reaction’ For Peer Corteva
detail:
FMC Stock Crashes 33% On Massive Earnings Downgrade – Citi expects ‘Modest Negative Reaction’ For Peer Corteva
Arnab Paul
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:10 AM PDT 4 min read
FMC
C
CTVA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The company also expects an adjusted EBITDA loss of $510 million to $565 million in Q3, compared to its earlier forecast of a $120 million to $140 million profit.

Citi said FMC's path to being free cash flow positive is 'increasingly uncertain.'

RBC Capital said FMC's full-year 2026 targets are at risk.

Shares of FMC Corporation (FMC) tumbled more than 33% on Thursday after the agricultural chemicals maker significantly cut its third-quarter earnings outlook amid inventory pressure and competition from cheaper generic products.

The update also raised concerns about peer Corteva (CTVA), with Citi expecting some negative fallout for the stock, although it sees Corteva as less exposed to generic competition.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

CTVA shares were down more than 4% at the time of writing.

FMC Slashes Revenue, Swings To Massive Loss

FMC now expects third-quarter (Q3) revenue between $65 million and $125 million, compared with its previous forecast of $840 million to $900 million, excluding India. The company also expects an adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) loss of $510 million to $565 million, compared to its earlier forecast of a $120 million to $140 million profit.

FMC said the forecast includes an estimated impact of $625 million to $675 million from lowering prices on select products in key markets and modifying its selling and pricing model in the United States.

FMC's Inventory Issues In Focus

FMC is facing slower-than-expected demand in key markets while distributors are holding higher-priced FMC products. The inventory was purchased under different cost structures and competitive conditions, the company said.

Rapid market price declines, driven in part by increased generic competition, have widened the valuation gap between the affected inventory and current market prices, making it difficult to sell the inventory.

FMC is considering two steps to address the bottleneck. The company is taking "comprehensive commercial actions" in Brazil, Argentina, the United States and Canada to lower the price of select products. It will also change its selling and pricing model in the United States.

The company expects to discuss potential changes to its debt agreements with lenders and provide an updated outlook when it reports earnings on October 29.

Citi Says Corteva Not As Exposed To Generic Pressure

Citi said that while FMC's actions could improve competitiveness, it sees "a challenging picture for the balance sheet into 2027," with FMC's path to free cash flow positivity "increasingly uncertain."

The firm expects a sharp negative reaction in FMC shares but "a modest negative reaction" in Corteva shares, saying Corteva's exposure to generic pressure is modest by comparison.

RBC Capital added that the change in Q3 outlook puts FMC's full-year 2026 targets at risk and is likely adding pressure on Corteva's stock.

Earlier this month, Corteva completed the spin-off of its seed business, Vylor (VYLR), with the company completely focused on crop protection. Corteva is targeting $8.4 billion to $8.7 billion in annual sales by 2029.

Retail's Take

Despite the crash, retail sentiment on Stocktwits surrounding FMC turned 'bullish' from 'neutral' a day earlier, amid a 300% jump in message volumes.

FMC.png

One user said that while FMC's actions could help the company survive bankruptcy, it would not become a $20 stock again.

FMC shares are down 62% so far in 2026.

title: JPMorgan vs. Citigroup: Which Stock Has the Edge After Q3 Results?
detail:
JPMorgan vs. Citigroup: Which Stock Has the Edge After Q3 Results?
Riya Anand
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:50 AM PDT 7 min read
JPM
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Banking giants JPMorgan JPM and Citigroup C kicked off the third-quarter earnings season this week with contrasting results amid an uncertain economic backdrop. While JPMorgan reinforced its position as an industry leader in profitability and financial strength despite earnings miss, Citigroup delivered robust earnings growth as its multiyear restructuring efforts continued to gain momentum.

Both banks benefited from stronger net interest income (NII), highlighting their resilience in an evolving operating environment. However, their investment propositions differ. JPMorgan's diversified business model, superior profitability, and solid balance sheet offer stability, while Citigroup's ongoing transformation, improving returns, and relatively attractive valuation could provide greater upside potential.

With both banking giants demonstrating resilience, which stock presents the more compelling investment opportunity following their Q3 earnings results? Let us compare their financial performance, growth prospects, and valuations to determine which bank may offer investors the better opportunity.

The Case for JPM

JPMorgan continues to benefit from its diversified business model, strong market position and consistent earnings-generating capabilities. Its leading consumer banking franchise, extensive credit card operations, investment banking and trading businesses, and expanding wealth management platform provide multiple revenue streams, helping it navigate changing economic conditions.

A major growth driver for JPMorgan remains its strong deposit franchise and expanding loan portfolio. In the third quarter, NII increased 13% year over year to $27.1 billion, supported by higher deposit balances, growth in credit card lending and increased wholesale loan activity. Excluding Markets, NII rose 6% to $24.7 billion, indicating continued underlying banking momentum.

Management projects 2026 NII of $106.2 billion. Its preliminary 2027 outlook calls for NII, excluding Markets, of $107 billion, supported by continued balance sheet expansion and higher interest rates. The Federal Reserve's 25-basis-point rate hike in September 2026 could provide an additional tailwind by supporting yields on floating-rate loans and interest-earning assets. However, higher deposit costs and the potential impact of elevated borrowing rates on loan demand could partially offset these benefits.

Prudent risk management and a strong balance sheet further support its long-term prospects. As of Sept. 30, 2026, the company maintained a standardized common equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio of 13.9%, backed by $304 billion in CET1 capital. It also held $1.5 trillion in cash and marketable securities, providing substantial liquidity to navigate economic uncertainty and support business expansion.

JPMorgan has a strong record of dividends and share repurchases, supported by its earnings strength and capital position. Over the past five years, the company has hiked its dividend six times and currently has a dividend yield of 1.9%. It also authorized a share repurchase program worth $50 billion. As of Sept. 30, 2026, JPMorgan had $48.94 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. Dividend Yield (TTM)

JPMorgan Chase & Co. Dividend Yield (TTM)

JPMorgan Chase & Co. dividend-yield-ttm | JPMorgan Chase & Co. Quote

Nevertheless, rising operating expenses remain concerning. Third-quarter expenses increased 12% year over year, outpacing revenue growth, reflecting higher compensation, technology spending and business expansion. Sustaining strong revenue momentum while maintaining expense discipline will be crucial for preserving its industry-leading profitability.

The Case for C

Citigroup offers a different investment proposition, centered on improving profitability, operational efficiency and unlocking value through its ongoing strategic transformation. The bank's globally diversified businesses, particularly Services, Markets, Wealth and Institutional Banking, provide a solid foundation for long-term growth.

Under CEO Jane Fraser, Citigroup has been working to simplify its organization. This includes exiting international consumer markets, streamlining operations, reducing management layers, cutting costs and focusing on higher-return businesses. The goal is to make C a leaner, more focused and profitable institution. Encouragingly, the transformation is beginning to deliver measurable improvements, with the company delivering positive operating leverage in the third quarter of 2026. Its efficiency ratio fell to 58.5% from 64.7% in the prior-year quarter, indicating improving profitability.

NII, excluding Markets, grew 7% year over year, reflecting strength in Services, Wealth and U.S. Consumer Cards. Management expects this metric to increase in the mid-to-high 6% range for 2026, complemented by continued non-interest revenue growth, excluding Markets. Supported by this momentum, management expects 2026 ROTCE to exceed 11%. Citigroup is targeting ROTCE of 11-13% for 2027-2028, with a longer-term objective of achieving sustainable returns of 14-15%. Successful execution of these targets could meaningfully strengthen earnings capacity and improve investor confidence.

Citigroup continues to prioritize shareholder returns while maintaining a solid capital position. As of Sept. 30, 2026, its Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio stood at 12.8%, approximately 120 basis points above the current regulatory requirement. Management also reaffirmed its commitment to the $30-billion share repurchase program announced at its May 2026 Investor Day. Over the past five years, the company has hiked its dividend four times, and has a dividend yield of 2.2%.

Citigroup Inc. Dividend Yield (TTM)
Citigroup Inc. Dividend Yield (TTM)

Citigroup Inc. dividend-yield-ttm | Citigroup Inc. Quote

However, Citigroup's transformation is not without challenges. Restructuring and technology modernization costs, regulatory compliance requirements, and credit risks in its consumer lending portfolio could weigh on profitability. Moreover, despite recent progress, its ROTCE remains significantly below JPMorgan's, highlighting the work that remains to achieve consistently competitive returns.

How Do Estimates Compare for Citigroup & JPMorgan?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for C's 2026 sales and EPS implies year-over-year increases of 12.1% and 40.5%, respectively. EPS estimates for 2026 have been revised upward over the past month.

Estimate Revision Trend

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for JPM's 2026 sales and EPS implies year-over-year increases of 13.9% and 15.9%, respectively. EPS estimates for 2026 have been revised upward over the past month.

Estimate Revision Trend

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

JPM & C: Stock Performance & Valuation Comparison

Over the past year, shares of JPMorgan have rallied 12.3%, whereas Citigroup has jumped 27%. This compares to the industry growth of 8.3%.

Price Performance

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

In terms of valuation, JPMorgan is currently trading at a 12-month forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 13.41X, higher than Citigroup's 9.74X and the industry average of 12.60X.

Price-to-Earnings F12M

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

JPMorgan's premium valuation reflects investors' confidence in its diversified business model, superior profitability, consistent execution and strong risk management capabilities. Its ability to generate robust returns across market cycles supports the higher multiple, although the premium may limit near-term upside potential.

Conversely, Citigroup's discounted valuation presents an opportunity for investors seeking greater upside potential. The bank's ongoing restructuring efforts, expense discipline and focus on improving returns could support a gradual valuation re-rating. However, the extent of this upside will depend on its ability to deliver sustained profitability improvements and execute its transformation initiatives effectively.

JPMorgan or Citigroup: Which Bank Has More Upside Potential?

Both JPM and C have demonstrated strong momentum in the third quarter, but their investment appeal differs. JPMorgan's diversified revenue streams, superior profitability, robust capital position and consistent shareholder returns make it a relatively stable investment choice. However, its premium valuation suggests that much of its operational strength is already reflected in the stock price.

Conversely, Citigroup offers greater potential for valuation upside, supported by improving profitability, ongoing restructuring initiatives and enhanced operating efficiency. Its relatively lower valuation leaves room for multiple expansion if management continues to deliver on its transformation goals. Nonetheless, execution risks remain, and achieving its long-term return targets will be crucial to sustaining investor confidence.

While JPMorgan appears better-positioned for investors prioritizing stability and consistent returns, Citigroup may appeal to those seeking higher turnaround-driven upside. For now, JPM and C both carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting investors may want to wait for more favorable earnings estimate revisions before aggressively adding positions.
